title: Autotune after-action synthesis and safe-deployments checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Synthesize learnings from the recent Optimize autotune incident and produce an operator-facing safe-deploy checklist and a concise after-action playbook that reduces blast radius for future autotune applies. This ticket covers the synthesis doc, automated canary gating rules, an operator checklist for manual approval, and the set of follow-up engineering tasks to harden the controller. Scope: batching/cache recommendation flow, staged apply orchestration, circuit-breaker thresholds, telemetries to validate cost/latency regressions, and an on-call rollback automation prototype.
postmortem_summary: On 2025-02-18 an autotune apply pushed a batched-caching profile that favored aggressive prefix caching and larger batch windows which reduced cost in simulations but increased tail latency for short requests under specific routing scenarios. We observed a gradual increase in 95th p99 latency and increased error rates for small-sequence traffic in US-West. The autotuner lacked a sliding window check for latency regressions during rollout and the staged-apply gate used only aggregate token-cost as a pass metric. Mitigation (manual rollback + partial failover to conservative profile) restored baseline within 22 minutes. No customer data was exposed, but customers experienced degraded latency for ~18 minutes.

root_causes: Release gating used aggregate cost delta only; lacked latency SLO gating for small-sequence traffic
Controller state machine allowed concurrent staged-progress transitions when telemetry was delayed
Simulation harness did not include representative short-seq traffic mix or the same routing sharding as production
No automated canary circuit-breaker for p95/p99 deltas; operator checklist omitted explicit hold-on-latency rule
mitigations_applied: Immediate manual rollback to conservative profile (applied by on-call)
Temporary canary freeze on autotune runs pending review
Emergency dashboard added to Console (optimize.autotune.last_apply) showing per-route p50/p95/p99 + cost delta
Owner: Marco Ruiz created a targeted simulation job reproducing the short-seq regression pattern

notes: Design trade-off: tightening latency gates increases chance to reject beneficial cost saves; we'll use staged canary + simulated ROI estimate rather than a single boolean cost gate
Operator checklist will require explicit confidence metrics (simulated cost, per-route p95, sample size >= 5000 requests)
We intend to run "simulation-mode" autotune weekly and compare the live canary telemetry before any live apply; this requires new telemetry labels from routing layer
Consider implementing "gamma gates": small UX-level knobs to defer aggressive caching on routes with high small-seq density
Prototype rollback automation will NOT auto-retry apply after rollback; retries require manual validation
